correctness.rationale: For the exact displayed sextic, the quartic square identity and A²−(t²+1)(t−1)²=t² imply four explicit distinct roots; the resultant 256(t−1)^4(t²−t+1)^4 excludes overlap with the other quadratic root pair. Thus the hyperelliptic cover is smooth of genus two. Differences of roots recover i and sqrt(t²+1), and the pair sqrt(−t) recovers sqrt(t), proving exact rather than upper-bounded splitting fields for both t and −t. Sign characters describe the entire Galois action; finite-field Frobenius then yields the two character formulas, cycle types and quadratic splitting. Identical curve zeta functions follow from the unpolarized Jacobian isomorphism proved in the cited source. The included executable checker exactly verifies identities, 488 parameter instances with paired point counts, and four selected quadratic splitting cases; those finite tests are not the proof of universal cases.

This is best-knowledge priority only and not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The intrinsically defined six Weierstrass points are natural arithmetic invariants for genus-two curves. This result completely computes the field generated by their supports and their Galois permutation representations for an entire published nontrivial family, then gives exact rational branch-point counts over every admissible odd finite field. The uniform 0-versus-2 difference for all q≡3 mod4 makes a sharp and mathematically motivated contrast between different curves with identical all-extension zeta functions. It is a full invariant classification, not an arbitrary finite census or rephrasing of the Jacobian-isomorphism input; the same splitting field shared by both partners adds useful structure.
